### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [qr-bracketedoptionlawtransport] Book: 50% SPY, 50% QQQ, bought at the first pass and left to drift; long only, no leverage. Events: FOMC statements (14:00 ET) and CPI releases (the BLS schedule); one is skipped when another FOMC, CPI or jobs release falls between 15:45 of its observation session and 09:35 of its exit session. Information: at 15:45 ET on the 5th session before the event and the session before that, for SPX (SPXW) and NDX (NDXP), the last expiry before and the first after the event (each within 4 sessions); two-sided calls with spreads ≤ 20% within ±10% of each expiry's put-call-parity forward (at least 9 strikes) bound the net up-crossing payoff (from at or below the forward to θ above it, less the reverse)
  - [qr-bracketedoptionlawtransport] 10. Execution in the code: rebalances go through the common helper from the first pass at or after 09:35, sells before buys (the card's marketable limits 1% through the quote, each good for 30 minutes, are the master-desk execution terms; the code's named divergence 5 records market orders on the desk's quotes). Named divergences 1-4 in the sleeve header stand: SPXW / NDXP cash-index options from CBOE delayed quotes replace CME E-mini options and futures; BLS schedules plus the desk FOMC list are the calendar; the strike grid is thinned as in step 3; training events accumulate from the sleeve's own snapshots only.
- Exit rules:
  - [qr-bracketedoptionlawtransport] Back to 50/50 at 09:35 ET of the 5th session after the event.
  - [qr-bracketedoptionlawtransport] 10. Execution in the code: rebalances go through the common helper from the first pass at or after 09:35, sells before buys (the card's marketable limits 1% through the quote, each good for 30 minutes, are the master-desk execution terms; the code's named divergence 5 records market orders on the desk's quotes). Named divergences 1-4 in the sleeve header stand: SPXW / NDXP cash-index options from CBOE delayed quotes replace CME E-mini options and futures; BLS schedules plus the desk FOMC list are the calendar; the strike grid is thinned as in step 3; training events accumulate from the sleeve's own snapshots only.
  - [qr-bracketedoptionlawtransport] - Back to 50/50 at 09:35 ET of the 5th session after the event.
- Sizing:
  - [qr-bracketedoptionlawtransport] Sleeve id: `qr_bracketedoptionlawtransport`; family quant_research; capital $1,000,000; cadence 300 seconds; schedule rth.
  - [qr-bracketedoptionlawtransport] Params (from the SleeveConfig): default weights SPY 0.5 / QQQ 0.5; tilts [0.25, 0.75] and [0.75, 0.25]; thetas [0.005, 0.01, 0.02]; ridge 100; exit_sessions 5; support [80, 40, 24]; margin_bp 50; cost_scenarios_bp [15, 30, 45]; drawdown_disable 0.25.
- Filters / data:
  - [qr-bracketedoptionlawtransport] 7. Model and admission (`decide_tilt`): matured events in time order split oldest-first into training (all but the last 64), calibration (40) and development (24); fewer than 80 training events fails the vendored `admission.physical_admission` support check and the book holds 50/50. The ridge (penalty 100, train-only standardisation, unpenalised intercept) is fitted on the training events and calibrated on the calibration residuals; forecast f for the new event; lower bound lcb = f - 1.645 x std(calibration residuals) / sqrt(n_cal). Incremental benefit per cost scenario c in (15, 30, 45) bp: 0.25 x |f| - 2 x c / 10000 x 0.25 must clear the ad
  - [qr-bracketedoptionlawtransport] Book: 50% SPY, 50% QQQ, bought at the first pass and left to drift; long only, no leverage. Events: FOMC statements (14:00 ET) and CPI releases (the BLS schedule); one is skipped when another FOMC, CPI or jobs release falls between 15:45 of its observation session and 09:35 of its exit session. ### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [apex-c3-follow-through] Trend score = the share of 6 bullish votes on the Nasdaq-100 total return (above its 50-, 100- and 200-day averages; up over 63, 126 and 252 days); volatility = a walk-forward HAR forecast of the next 5 days. APEX-50F: exposure = trend score × min(4, 50% / volatility). Follow-through: once the Nasdaq-100 closes 10% under its 63-day high, the first session up ≥ 1.25% that closes at a 10-day high lifts exposure to at least 2× for 20 sessions; one per correction, re-armed after a new 63-day high. Decided on the last finished session; the held exposure moves to the target only on a change of 0.20 or more, or to 0.
- Exit rules:
  - [apex-c3-follow-through] The boost ends after 20 sessions; no stop. - No stop: exposure follows the target; a trend score of 0 holds only T-bills (BIL).
  - [apex-c3-follow-through] 2. Follow-through mask: arm when the Nasdaq-100 level closes at or below its 63-day high x (1 - 0.10); re-arm only after a new 63-day high. While armed and not yet used, the first session with a daily return >= 1.25% that closes at its 10-day high triggers the boost; one follow-through per correction.
  - [apex-c3-follow-through] - The boost ends after 20 sessions; no stop. - No stop: exposure follows the target; a trend score of 0 holds only T-bills (BIL).

  - [apex-c3-follow-through] Shares = floor(weight × book equity / the last close), frozen per decision; a $100,000 book; debits pay 7.75% a year.

Variance Value, at a month's first session with none held, on the next monthly expiry ≥ 15 days out: at-the-money implied vol / the HAR forecast ≥ 1.25 sells the at-the-money straddle and buys wings 1.5 σ√T out (an iron fly), NAV / spot shares a leg; ≤ 0.95 buys the at-the-money straddle with 2% of NAV.
  - [apex-o10-leaps-vv] 4. Variance Value, at a month's first session with none held, on the next monthly expiry >= 15 days out: at-the-money implied vol / the HAR forecast >= 1.25 sells the at-the-money straddle and buys wings 1.5 sigma sqrt(T) out (an iron fly), NAV / spot shares a leg; <= 0.95 buys the at-the-money straddle with 2% of NAV.
- Exit rules:
  - [apex-o10-leaps-vv] L* ≤ 0 sells the calls; rolled under 183 days or outside 0.60-0.95 delta; the Variance Value structures are held to expiry.
  - [apex-o10-leaps-vv] 4. Variance Value, at a month's first session with none held, on the next monthly expiry >= 15 days out: at-the-money implied vol / the HAR forecast >= 1.25 sells the at-the-money straddle and buys wings 1.5 sigma sqrt(T) out (an iron fly), NAV / spot shares a leg; <= 0.95 buys the at-the-money straddle with 2% of NAV.
  - [apex-o10-leaps-vv] - L* ≤ 0 sells the calls; rolled under 183 days or outside 0.60-0.95 delta; the Variance Value structures are held to expiry.
- Sizing:
  - [apex-o10-leaps-vv] 6. Sizing: Core: T-bills (BIL). Options decide once a session in the last 45 minutes (15:15-15:45 ET): the listed QQQ monthly and strike nearest the model's, whole contracts (under one skipped), a structure as one multi-leg package, marketable limits. The core trades market-on-close on the equity less the options' value. Book $1,000,000 for this options study (see Configuration).
- Filters / data:
  - [apex-o10-leaps-vv] - Yahoo full daily histories: ^NDX and QQQ (the Nasdaq-100 total return), ^IRX (T-bills); recomputed after each close. The live QQQ quote and option chain; a model surface from VXN and the VIX 9-day / 3-month / 6-month ratios at today's levels; Black-Scholes with a 0.55% dividend.

  - L* = the APEX-50F target on the last finished session (trend score × min(4, 50% / volatility)).

- Created by / source: Milkman Trades (milkmantrades.com), Daily Bilbo Boxes on Saty's compression; the Milkman v2 study
- Description (from source records): Daily Bilbo Box
- Algorithm status: **FULL**
- Algorithm sources consulted: Test catalog entry/variants, Test strategies/milkman/mk-dailybilbobox.md, docs/MK_DAILYBILBOBOX-RECREATE.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test strategies/milkman/mk-dailybilbobox.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test (main) strategies/milkman/mk-dailybilbobox.md — section '## Exit', Test strategies/milkman/mk-dailybilbobox.md (Sizing section), Test docs/verify/milkman.md, Test docs/MK_DAILYBILBOBOX-RECREATE.md (Full algorithm section), Test strategies/milkman/mk-dailybilbobox.md (Entry section), Test strategies/milkman/mk-dailybilbobox.md (Exit section), 2026-10-31 algorithm audit cure A (findings b1-entry, b2-exit, b3-sizing, b5-reconcile; quotes verbatim from cited sources)

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [mk-dailybilbobox] Squeeze (Saty's compression): the 21-day, 2-sd Bollinger band inside 2 × ATR(14) around EMA(21), not while the gap widens inside 1.854 × ATR. Box: the high and low of a squeeze's first 5 bars (fewer if it ends sooner), locked at the 5th bar or at its end. For 20 bars after the lock: buys when the high reaches the box high with the prior close above EMA(21) (short: the low through the box low, the prior close below EMA21), at max(open, box high); void once the other side is reached first. One trade at a time per symbol and side. Stocks trade only while their 20-day mean dollar volume is ≥ $5M and the close ≥ $3.
  - [mk-dailybilbobox] Boxes the first 5 days of a daily squeeze, buys a break above the box (shorts a break below) and trails the stop along the 50-day EMA. Note on the card: a related long-only desk sleeve trades this box with a nowcast arm and earnings exits; that sleeve is a different strategy and is not this package.
- Exit rules:
  - [mk-dailybilbobox] Stop at the box's other side, ratcheted each bar to the prior bar's EMA(50), never back; the entry bar stops only on a close through it; out after 250 bars.
  - [mk-dailybilbobox] Boxes the first 5 days of a daily squeeze, buys a break above the box (shorts a break below) and trails the stop along the 50-day EMA. Note on the card: a related long-only desk sleeve trades this box with a nowcast arm and earnings exits; that sleeve is a different strategy and is not this package.
  - [mk-dailybilbobox] - Stop at the box's other side, ratcheted each bar to the prior bar's EMA(50), never back; the entry bar stops only on a close through it; out after 250 bars.
- Sizing:
  - [mk-dailybilbobox] $10,000 a trade on a $1,000,000 book, every signal taken; each lane keeps its own trades and the sleeve trades the net per symbol.
  - [mk-dailybilbobox] | Entry: Stocks trade only while their 20-day mean dollar volume is ≥ $5M and the close ≥ $3. | `sleeves/milkman/vendor/milkman/dlib.py:23-26`<br>`sleeves/milkman/vendor/milkma
  - [mk-dailybilbobox] 7. Execution / sizing: close rules are decided 15 to 11 minutes before the close on the bar so far and sent market-on-close; level touches trade at the market when seen; signals of the completed bar trade at the next open. $10,000 a trade on a $1,000,000 book, every signal taken; each lane keeps its own trades and the sleeve trades the net per symbol. ### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [mk-tenminutecompressionrelease] Saty's compression on 10-minute candles; the first candle out of a squeeze whose preceding squeeze run is at least N candles: N=3 for the long lane, N=18 for the short lane (code cells in sleeves/milkman/intraday.py, setup COMP10). - Type: other | Family: unrecorded | Style evidence (catalog): not recorded

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [TRADER_SQUEEZE20] Squeeze definition (period 20): Bollinger Bands BB(20, 2, population stdev) around the 20-period SMA; Keltner Channel KC(20, 1.5 x ATR) around EMA(20) with Wilder/RMA ATR; a bar is in squeeze when the BB lower band is above the KC lower band and the BB upper band is below the KC upper band. Momentum is the LazyBear momentum: the linear-regression endpoint of the last 20 values of delta, where delta = close - ((20-bar high/low midpoint + SMA20) / 2). Entry (all must hold on a completed daily bar): the prior bar was in squeeze and the current bar is not; momentum > 0 and momentum > the prior bar's momentum; close > the prior 20-day high (the maximum high of the 20 bars before the current bar).
- Exit rules:
  - [TRADER_SQUEEZE20] 2. Entry (all must hold on a completed daily bar): the prior bar was in squeeze and the current bar is not; momentum > 0 and momentum > the prior bar's momentum; close > the prior 20-day high (the maximum high of the 20 bars before the current bar). Features require at least 252 daily bars, and the desk port drops bars dated the current session from the feature set (completed-bar rule). 3. Exit (first that fires): close < EMA20 (the Keltner centre); momentum <= 0; the initial 2 x ATR(14) stop is touched (the bar's low against the stop price recorded at entry, entry close minus 2 x ATR(14)); or 20 completed holding bars.
- Sizing:
  - [TRADER_SQUEEZE20] Sizing and slot limit: algorithm step 4. State: per-symbol entry bar count and stop price, kept by the engine's state store.
- Filters / data:
  - [TRADER_SQUEEZE20] Squeeze definition (period 20): Bollinger Bands BB(20, 2, population stdev) around the 20-period SMA; Keltner Channel KC(20, 1.5 x ATR) around EMA(20) with Wilder/RMA ATR; a bar is in squeeze when the BB lower band is above the KC lower band and the BB upper band is below the KC upper band. Momentum is the LazyBear momentum: the linear-regression endpoint of the last 20 values of delta, where delta = close - ((20-bar high/low midpoint + SMA20) / 2). Entry (all must hold on a completed daily bar): the prior bar was in squeeze and the current bar is not; momentum > 0 and momentum > the prior bar's momentum; close > the prior 20-day high (the maximum high of the 20 bars before the current bar).
- Parameters:
  - Universe: the 15 ETFs in step 5. Timeframe: 1d. Asset class: US ETFs. Cadence: 300 seconds in regular trading hours (code spec).

- Sizing:
  - [apex-c2-sector-kings] 5. Sizing: sector ETFs one for one (up to 2x in all, on margin); idle capital in BIL. Shares = floor(weight x book equity / the last close), frozen per decision; debits pay 7.75% a year.

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [apex-e7-turn-of-month] Trend score = the share of 6 bullish votes on the Nasdaq-100 total return (above its 50-, 100- and 200-day averages; up over 63, 126 and 252 days); volatility = a walk-forward HAR forecast of the next 5 days. APEX-30: exposure = trend score × min(3, 30% / volatility), + 0.5 held over the turn of the month (its last session and the next month's first three) while the trend score is ≥ 0.5, at most 3×. Decided on the last finished session; the held exposure moves to the target only on a change of 0.20 or more, or to 0.
- Exit rules:
  - [apex-e7-turn-of-month] The 0.5× leaves after the month's third session; no stop.
  - [apex-e7-turn-of-month] 4. Exit: the 0.5x leaves after the month's third session; no stop.
  - [apex-e7-turn-of-month] - The 0.5× leaves after the month's third session; no stop.
- Sizing:
  - [apex-e7-turn-of-month] 5. Sizing: market-on-close in the next session (orders from the open to 20 minutes before the close): Nasdaq exposure up to 1x is QQQ, 1-3x is QQQ + TQQQ (QQQ + 3 x TQQQ = L), above 3x TQQQ alone at L / 3 on margin; idle capital in BIL. Shares = floor(weight x book equity / the last close), frozen per decision; debits pay 7.75% a year.
- Filters / data:
  - [apex-e7-turn-of-month] Trend score = the share of 6 bullish votes on the Nasdaq-100 total return (above its 50-, 100- and 200-day averages; up over 63, 126 and 252 days); volatility = a walk-forward HAR forecast of the next 5 days. Decided on the last finished session; the held exposure moves to the target only on a change of 0.20 or more, or to 0.
- Parameters:
  - Trend score = the share of 6 bullish votes on the Nasdaq-100 total return (above its 50-, 100- and 200-day averages; up over 63, 126 and 252 days); volatility = a walk-forward HAR forecast of the next 5 days.
  - APEX-30: exposure = trend score × min(3, 30% / volatility), + 0.5 held over the turn of the month (its last session and the next month's first three) while the trend score is ≥ 0.5, at most 3×.

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [r17-etf-ladder] Month-end decision; signals: 126- and 21-day log returns, 63-day volatility, 200-day MA, 20-day drawdown. LEADER3: top 3 by 126-day return. RELATIVE3: top 3 beating QQQ. VOLADJ3: relative strength / volatility. ACCEL3: (21-day - 126-day/6) / volatility, above the 200-day MA. REPAIR3: beating QQQ, 2-10% off the 20-day high, up 3 days, above the 200-day MA. ESCAPE1: best positive 126-day return above the 200-day MA. Unfilled slots go to QQQ (ESCAPE1 stays in cash).
  - [r17-etf-ladder] 4. Execution (wrapper book law for the protocol's primary cell): pending weights x gross become desired units at the next open, from that open's marks and the pretrade NAV; desired units persist until the next decision. Each open: sells first. Each fund is capped at 0.1% of its prior-session raw dollar volume, the cap shared by sells then buys; buys are scaled to settled cash / (1 + cost). Sale proceeds settle T+1 and cannot be spent before then. Units are fractional. Each side costs 15 bps.
- Exit rules:
  - [r17-etf-ladder] Held to the next month-end decision; sells first at the open.
  - [r17-etf-ladder] 4. Execution (wrapper book law for the protocol's primary cell): pending weights x gross become desired units at the next open, from that open's marks and the pretrade NAV; desired units persist until the next decision. Each open: sells first. Each fund is capped at 0.1% of its prior-session raw dollar volume, the cap shared by sells then buys; buys are scaled to settled cash / (1 + cost). Sale proceeds settle T+1 and cannot be spent before then. Units are fractional. Each side costs 15 bps.
  - [r17-etf-ladder] - Held to the next month-end decision; sells first at the open.
- Sizing:
  - [r17-etf-ladder] 6. Sizing: equal weights x gross 0.98; cash account; $100,000 book (the primary cell recorded in the wrapper header).
  - [r17-etf-ladder] Six sleeves, one per rule: r17_leader3, r17_relative3, r17_voladj3, r17_accel3, r17_repair3 (3 slots each), r17_escape1 (1 slot).
- Filters / data:
  - [r17-etf-ladder] - Total-return (all-adjusted) daily closes and raw dollar volume for the universe, on QQQ's session axis; 252 QQQ sessions required through the signal close.

- Type: market timing and rotation | Family: midna | Style evidence (catalog): Trend filter

- Timeframe: 1w
- Created by / source: Midna's TypeScript desk (equity books), ported line for line to the master desk
- Description (from source records): QLD weekly timing
- Algorithm status: **FULL**
- Algorithm sources consulted: Test catalog entry/variants, Test strategies/midna/mn-qld-weekly-timing.md, docs/MN_QLD_WEEKLY_TIMING-RECREATE.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test strategies/midna/mn-qld-weekly-timing.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test (main) strategies/midna/mn-qld-weekly-timing.md — section '## Exit', Test docs/MN_QLD_WEEKLY_TIMING-RECREATE.md (Configuration section), Test strategies/midna/mn-qld-weekly-timing.md (Entry section), Test strategies/midna/mn-qld-weekly-timing.md (Exit section), Test strategies/midna/mn-qld-weekly-timing.md (summary line), Test docs/verify/midna.md, 2026-10-31 algorithm audit cure A (findings b1-entry, b2-exit, b3-sizing, b5-reconcile; quotes verbatim from cited sources)

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [mn-qld-weekly-timing] Prior completed QQQ week: EMA(12) above EMA(26) of weekly closes (SMA-seeded, from 1990 adjusted daily history). Trades in the first regular-hours pass of the week.
  - [mn-qld-weekly-timing] 4. Entry: if on and QLD is not held, enter QLD at the live quote (ask or last), notional = cash / (1 + 0.1%); cost parameter COST = 0.001; book capital in code NAV = 100,000.
- Exit rules:
  - [mn-qld-weekly-timing] Sells QLD at the open of a week whose prior week shows EMA(12) ≤ EMA(26).
  - [mn-qld-weekly-timing] 5. Exit: if not on (EMA(12) <= EMA(26)) and QLD is held, sell QLD at bid or last in that first pass of the week.
  - [mn-qld-weekly-timing] - Sells QLD at the open of a week whose prior week shows EMA(12) ≤ EMA(26).
- Sizing:
  - [mn-qld-weekly-timing] Capital in code: 100,000. Cadence 300s, schedule rth, needs quotes for QLD and feed `midna_qld_daily`.
- Filters / data:
  - [mn-qld-weekly-timing] - Yahoo QQQ and QLD daily history (adjusted, from 1990-01-01 as fetched by the producer feed in the code docstring).
- Parameters:
  - Prior completed QQQ week: EMA(12) above EMA(26) of weekly closes (SMA-seeded, from 1990 adjusted daily history).
  - Sells QLD at the open of a week whose prior week shows EMA(12) ≤ EMA(26).
  - Holds QLD all-in while QQQ's weekly EMA(12) is above its EMA(26), switching at the open of each week.

## O'Neil follow-through-day race

- Type: market timing and rotation | Family: milkman | Style evidence (catalog): Market-timing breakout
- Trades: US index ETFs and futures — 14 index ETFs and futures
- Timeframe: 1d
- Created by / source: William O'Neil's follow-through day, as coded by the Milkman v2 study
- Description (from source records): O'Neil follow-through-day race
- Algorithm status: **FULL**
- Algorithm sources consulted: Test catalog entry/variants, Test strategies/milkman/mk-oneilfollowthroughdayrace.md, docs/MK_ONEILFOLLOWTHROUGHDAYRACE-RECREATE.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test strategies/milkman/mk-oneilfollowthroughdayrace.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test (main) strategies/milkman/mk-oneilfollowthroughdayrace.md — section '## Exit', Test docs/MK_ONEILFOLLOWTHROUGHDAYRACE-RECREATE.md, Test docs/CATALOG.json entry for mk-oneilfollowthroughdayrace, 2026-10-31 algorithm audit cure A (findings b1-entry, b2-exit, b3-sizing, b5-reconcile; quotes verbatim from cited sources)

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [mk-oneilfollowthroughdayrace] Correction: a close 10% under the highest close of the last 63; the lowest low since is the correction low. Rally: the first up close is day 1; a low under day 1's low restarts the count; from day 4, a close up ≥ 1.25% on higher volume than the day before is the follow-through day; enters at its close. A close back within 0.1% of the 63-day high resets it.
  - [mk-oneilfollowthroughdayrace] 2. Rally: the first up close is day 1; a low under day 1's low restarts the count; from day 4, a close up >= 1.25% on higher volume than the day before is the follow-through day; enter at its close. Distance = close - correction low.
- Exit rules:
  - [mk-oneilfollowthroughdayrace] Long: target close + (close - correction low), stop the correction low. Short: target the correction low, stop close + the same distance. From the next bar, stop first; else out at the close after 120 sessions.
  - [mk-oneilfollowthroughdayrace] 4. Exit, long row: target close + distance, stop the correction low. Short row: target the correction low, stop close + distance. From the next bar, stop is checked first; otherwise exit at the close after 120 sessions.
  - [mk-oneilfollowthroughdayrace] - Long: target close + (close - correction low), stop the correction low. Short: target the correction low, stop close + the same distance. From the next bar, stop first; else out at the close after 120 sessions.
- Sizing:

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:

Budget: a point each for SPY under its 26-week average, a 13-week drawdown ≥ 10% and a VIX robust z-score (3 years) ≥ 3; 0 points invests 100%, 1 point 85%, 2-3 points 70%; 70% too when SPY or QQQ fell ≥ 3% over 3 sessions, or when the VIX z-score is ≥ 3 and its change's ≥ 3.5. Groups: growth tech (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, META, AMZN, GOOGL, TSLA), real assets (XOM, CVX, COP, FCX, BHP, GLD, SLV) and defensive (TLT, IEF, XLU, XLV, IAU, SHY, UUP), ranked by 12-week information ratio against QQQ; the best two that beat
  - [qr-finrlxreleasedadaptiverotationrecons] 7. Orders (card): marketable limits 1% through the quote, each good for 30 minutes; sells first, buys once no sell is outstanding. Wrapper divergence recorded in its docstring: the rebalance trades at the market from the first pass of the session after the decision Friday, sized on the live quote and the sleeve's NAV; sells first and buys follow on the next pass once no sell is outstanding.
- Exit rules:
  - [qr-finrlxreleasedadaptiverotationrecons] Names outside the new week's allocation are sold at that rebalance; holdings drift between Fridays.

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [R19_ETF_INTERVAL1_M150] ausar variant: ETF leader confirmed across two sources · 150% exposure
  - [ausar_pb90] Calculates each ETF’s completed 126-session return separately from Alpaca and Yahoo. The two values form a range. A new leader is chosen only when its lower return exceeds every competitor’s higher return. When ranges overlap, retain the incumbent if it is still a possible winner; otherwise select QQQ. Allocates to the selected fund. Targets ETF holdings worth 150% of the paper account's net value
  - [ausar_r19_R19_ETF_INTERVAL1_M150] Calculates each ETF’s completed 126-session return separately from Alpaca and Yahoo. The two values form a range. A new leader is chosen only when its lower return exceeds every competitor’s higher return. When ranges overlap, retain the incumbent if it is still a possible winner; otherwise select QQQ. Allocates to the selected fund. Targets ETF holdings worth 150% of the paper account's net value
- Exit rules:
  - [ausar_pb90] Reduce or replace holdings when the next monthly selection changes their target. This strategy has no price-based stop or profit target.
  - [ausar_r19_R19_ETF_INTERVAL1_M150] Reduce or replace holdings when the next monthly selection changes their target. This strategy has no price-based stop or profit target.
- Sizing:
  - [R19_ETF_INTERVAL1_M150] Sizing: desired shares = floor(weight x gross x NAV / price), whole shares, never capped inside the sleeve. Price is the last close, falling back to the position average price for a held symbol with no bars. If any needed price is at or below zero, the sleeve emits nothing.
- Filters / data:
  - [ausar_pb90] data: Completed historical ETF bars for signals; separately labeled IEX quotes for execution. The two-source versions compare complete Alpaca and Yahoo histories without joining them.
  - [ausar_r19_R19_ETF_INTERVAL1_M150] data: posted r19 data adapters

- Type: crypto basis and funding | Family: milkman | Style evidence (catalog): Rule basket

- Timeframe: 1d
- Created by / source: The Milkman v2 study's crypto variant, on Galath research's crypto-linked stock list
- Description (from source records): Milkman daily rules on crypto-linked stocks
- Algorithm status: **FULL**

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [mk-milkmancryptolinkedstockvariant] Rules: Connors Double 7 (7, SMA200), Legend's Buy Day overnight (3), Daily Bilbo Box (5, EMA50 trail), Swing and Multi-day Golden Gates, EMA21 deviation (2 ATR, 10 sessions), Phase Oscillator accumulation (20 sessions), Pivot Ribbon 13/48, compression expansion (10 bars, 5 sessions); each long and short. Names: the crypto-linked stock list's symbols among the 1,822 stocks (134). Stocks trade only while their 20-day mean dollar volume is ≥ $5M and the close ≥ $3.
  - [mk-milkmancryptolinkedstockvariant] Runs nine of the study's daily rules, long and short, on 134 crypto-linked US stocks.
- Exit rules:
  - [mk-milkmancryptolinkedstockvariant] Each rule exits by its own rule: a 7-day closing extreme, the next open, the EMA50 trail, a gate target, stop or period end, an EMA21 touch, a fixed hold, the opposite cross.
  - [mk-milkmancryptolinkedstockvariant] 3. Exit: each rule exits by its own rule: a 7-day closing extreme, the next open, the EMA50 trail, a gate target, stop or period end, an EMA21 touch, a fixed hold, the opposite cross.
  - [mk-milkmancryptolinkedstockvariant] - Each rule exits by its own rule: a 7-day closing extreme, the next open, the EMA50 trail, a gate target, stop or period end, an EMA21 touch, a fixed hold, the opposite cross.
- Sizing:
  - [mk-milkmancryptolinkedstockvariant] 4. Sizing: Close rules are decided 15 to 11 minutes before the close on the bar so far and sent market-on-close; level touches trade at the market when seen; signals of the completed bar trade at the next open. $10,000 a trade on a $1,000,000 book, every signal taken; each lane keeps its own trades and the sleeve trades the net per symbol. Futures lanes trade on a simulated venue quoted from Yahoo, or are only recorded where that venue has no quote.
- Filters / data:
  - [mk-milkmancryptolinkedstockvariant] 1. Universe filter: the crypto-linked stock list's symbols among the 1,822 stocks (134 names). Stocks trade only while their 20-day mean dollar volume is >= $5M and the close >= $3.
  - [mk-milkmancryptolinkedstockvariant] Rules: Connors Double 7 (7, SMA200), Legend's Buy Day overnight (3), Daily Bilbo Box (5, EMA50 trail), Swing and Multi-day Golden Gates, EMA21 deviation (2 ATR, 10 sessions), Phase Oscillator accumulation (20 sessions), Pivot Ribbon 13/48, compression expansion (10 bars, 5 sessions); each long and short. Names: the crypto-linked stock list's symbols among the 1,822 stocks (134). Stocks trade only while their 20-day mean dollar volume is ≥ $5M and the close ≥ $3.

  - Rules: Connors Double 7 (7, SMA200), Legend's Buy Day overnight (3), Daily Bilbo Box (5, EMA50 trail), Swing and Multi-day Golden Gates, EMA21 deviation (2 ATR, 10 sessions), Phase Oscillator accumulation (20 sessions), Pivot Ribbon 13/48, compression expansion (10 bars, 5 sessions); each long and short.

  - [ausar_pb127] Builds the canonical M2-qualified weekly cohort, compares it with SPY and selects the configured beta cohort after consolidating issuer aliases. It is a relative-market selection experiment, not a guarantee of market outperformance.

  - [R19_TENSOR_BETA_M2_52W_25] 5. Sizing: accounting ticket 4000 with fee_bps 10; Test implementation qty = floor($400 / entry price) (the scaled ticket), qty < 1 emits nothing.

### Detailed algorithm

## APEX N6: GESTALT × APEX

- Type: forecast and ML models | Family: apex | Style evidence (catalog): Trend × volatility + analog forecast
- Trades: US ETFs (incl. 3× leveraged) — QQQ, TQQQ, BIL
- Timeframe: 1d
- Created by / source: APEX research desk (Cursor2), invention N6
- Description (from source records): APEX N6: GESTALT × APEX
- Algorithm status: **FULL**
- Algorithm sources consulted: Test catalog entry/variants, Test strategies/apex/apex-n6-gestalt-apex.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test strategies/apex/apex-n6-gestalt-apex.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test (main) strategies/apex/apex-n6-gestalt-apex.md — section '## Exit', docs/APEX_N6_GESTALT_APEX-RECREATE.md, Test strategies/apex/apex-n6-gestalt-apex.md (Sizing section), Test docs/APEX_N6_GESTALT_APEX-RECREATE.md (Full algorithm section), Test docs/APEX_N6_GESTALT_APEX-RECREATE.md (Configuration section), 2026-10-31 algorithm audit cure A (findings b1-entry, b2-exit, b3-sizing, b5-reconcile; quotes verbatim from cited sources)

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [apex-n6-gestalt-apex] Trend score = the share of 6 bullish votes on the Nasdaq-100 total return (above its 50-, 100- and 200-day averages; up over 63, 126 and 252 days); volatility = a walk-forward HAR forecast of the next 5 days. Exposure = ½ × (APEX-50F target + GESTALT leverage). GESTALT: half-Kelly on the mean forward 21-day excess return of the 150 most similar past states, refit every 5 sessions, 0-4. Decided on the last finished session; the held exposure moves to the target only on a change of 0.20 or more, or to 0.
- Exit rules:
  - [apex-n6-gestalt-apex] No stop: exposure follows the target; a trend score of 0 holds only T-bills (BIL).
  - [apex-n6-gestalt-apex] 6. Exit: no stop. Exposure follows the target; a trend score of 0 holds only BIL.
  - [apex-n6-gestalt-apex] - No stop: exposure follows the target; a trend score of 0 holds only T-bills (BIL).
- Sizing:
  - [apex-n6-gestalt-apex] Shares = floor(weight × book equity / the last close), frozen per decision; a $100,000 book; debits pay 7.75% a year.
  - [apex-n6-gestalt-apex] 7. Execution/sizing: market-on-close in the next session (orders from the open to 20 minutes before the close). Nasdaq exposure up to 1x is QQQ; 1-3x is QQQ + TQQQ with QQQ + 3 x TQQQ = L; above 3x TQQQ alone at L/3 on margin; idle capital in BIL. Shares = floor(weight x book equity / last close), frozen per decision; $100,000 book; debits pay 7.75% a year.
- Filters / data:
  - [apex-n6-gestalt-apex] Trend score = the share of 6 bullish votes on the Nasdaq-100 total return (above its 50-, 100- and 200-day averages; up over 63, 126 and 252 days); volatility = a walk-forward HAR forecast of the next 5 days. Exposure = ½ × (APEX-50F target + GESTALT leverage). GESTALT: half-Kelly on the mean forward 21-day excess return of the 150 most similar past states, refit every 5 sessions, 0-4. Decided on the last finished session; the held exposure moves to the target only on a change of 0.20 or more, or to 0.
- Parameters:
  - GESTALT: k=150 neighbours, refit every 5 sessions, shrink 0.5, leverage clipped 0-4, start 2001-01-02 in the N5/GESTALT defaults used by the ensemble.

- Type: forecast and ML models | Family: ausar | Style evidence (catalog): Momentum repair
- Trades: US equities — 1,820 hourly / 1,813 weekly names
- Timeframe: 1h · 1w
- Created by / source: Ausar R11 Tensor state research
- Description (from source records): Tensor state repair (hourly / weekly)
- Algorithm status: **FULL**
- Algorithm sources consulted: Test catalog entry/variants, muse-desk-v3 roster params/slice, Test docs/ASTER_TENSOR_H1_RECOVERY-ALGORITHM.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test docs/ASTER_TENSOR_H1_RECOVERY-ALGORITHM.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test (main) docs/ASTER_TENSOR_H1_RECOVERY-ALGORITHM.md — section '## Exit rules', Test docs/ASTER_TENSOR_H1_RECOVERY-RECREATE.md (Configuration section), Test docs/ASTER_TENSOR_H1_RECOVERY-ALGORITHM.md (Spec section), 2026-10-31 algorithm audit cure A (findings b1-entry, b2-exit, b3-sizing, b5-reconcile; quotes verbatim from cited sources)

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [tensor-state-repair] Exits are evaluated first; if any exit intent is emitted, the call returns exits only. A symbol needs at least a 4-bar panel on the sleeve's frame. Repair test on the last 4 bars: balance[-1] - balance[0] >= 2; at least 2 of the 7 vote channels strictly increase across at least one adjacent transition in the panel; total_votes == 7 at both panel ends; the latest row's native status, when present, must be "ready". Price/volume gates on the latest panel row: close >= 5, dollar_volume20 >= 1,000,000, atr14 > 0. Warmup: the current bar index + 1 must be >= 234 (minimum source bars). Cooldown: 20 native bars after an entry (the sleeve's state file records next_eligible_bar_index = entry bar index
- Exit rules:
  - [tensor-state-repair] The only designed exit is time: a position is sold in full when the current panel bar index minus its entry bar index reaches 20 native bars (late observation still exits). The exit price is the latest bar close on the sleeve's timeframe when available. - No price stop and no profit target in the source policy.
  - [tensor-state-repair] - The only designed exit is time: a position is sold in full when the current panel bar index minus its entry bar index reaches 20 native bars (late observation still exits). The exit price is the latest bar close on the sleeve's timeframe when available. - No price stop and no profit target in the source policy.
- Sizing:
  - [aster_tensor_h1_recovery] v3 slice: {"capital_usd": 10000.0, "cash_usd": 10000.0} parked=False
  - [aster_tensor_w1_recovery] v3 slice: {"capital_usd": 10000.0, "cash_usd": 10000.0} parked=False
- Filters / data:
  - [tensor-state-repair] Exits are evaluated first; if any exit intent is emitted, the call returns exits only. A symbol needs at least a 4-bar panel on the sleeve's frame. Repair test on the last 4 bars: balance[-1] - balance[0] >= 2; at least 2 of the 7 vote channels strictly increase across at least one adjacent transition in the panel; total_votes == 7 at both panel ends; the latest row's native status, when present, must be "ready". Price/volume gates on the latest panel row: close >= 5, dollar_volume20 >= 1,000,000, atr14 > 0. Warmup: the current bar index + 1 must be >= 234 (minimum source bars). Cooldown: 20 native bars after an entry (the sleeve's state file records next_eligible_bar_index = entry bar index
- Parameters:
  - Sizing / slice: capital_usd 10000.0, cash_usd 10000.0; budget and share formula in the Full algorithm section; 10 slots; bp_buffer_frac=0.02.
  - kind="tensor", frame="1h", tf="1Hour", cadence_s=3600, session="rth". - Inputs (INPUTS_BY_KIND["tensor"]): tensor, bars, positions. - Vote channels (7): stoch, aroon, di, obv, squeeze, pivot, wave. A panel row's balance is bullish votes minus bearish votes (or the row's own balance field); excluded symbols: SPY, QQQ, B, GOLD. At most 10 positions are held (free = 10 - held).

  - [qr-newsconditioned121leadership] 6. Sizing: $1,000,000 book: 0.5% of NAV at risk to the stop per entry, <= 10% of NAV a name, <= 30% a sector, <= 2% of NAV total stop risk, at most 8 names.

## Tensor 1H Swing (v615)

- Type: forecast and ML models | Family: tensor_research | Style evidence (catalog): Swing confirmation
- Trades: US equities — 1,838-name genome roster
- Timeframe: 1h
- Created by / source: FolioTend v615 Tensor Swing (full-universe study) and its corrected 10 / 20 / 30-bar winner census, as forward-test books
- Description (from source records): Tensor 1H Swing (v615)
- Algorithm status: **FULL**
- Algorithm sources consulted: Test catalog entry/variants, Test strategies/tensor_research/tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615.md, docs/TR_RO_TENSOR_1H_SWING_V615-RECREATE.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test strategies/tensor_research/tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test (main) strategies/tensor_research/tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615.md — section '## Exit', Test docs/TR_RO_TENSOR_1H_SWING_V615-RECREATE.md, Test docs/TR_RO_TENSOR_1H_SWING_V615-RECREATE.md (Configuration section), 2026-10-31 algorithm audit cure A (findings b1-entry, b2-exit, b3-sizing, b5-reconcile; quotes verbatim from cited sources)

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615] Setup, a black square: an hourly bar with no primary marker, ≥ 5 of 7 bullish votes, the fast state bullish and the slow not; confirmation, a green arrow (≥ 5 bullish votes, ≥ 4 more than bearish) on the current completed hour within 3 bars of the setup; one episode per setup bar. Fired once per notification episode; the census book splits each episode into three equal sub-lots. Only the bar just completed counts, and the roster's run publishes once at least half its names reach it. Entry: the next hour's open, a market order within that hour; skipped once it has passed.
  - [tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615] A forward-test book over the 1,838-name genome roster on completed hourly bars: when a Tensor black-square setup is confirmed by a green arrow within 3 bars, buy at the next hour's open and sell at the close of hour 20. The winner-census book trades the same deduplicated episodes in three equal sub-lots closing at hours 10, 20 and 30. Modeled cost 25.5 bp a side.
- Exit rules:
  - [tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615] Exit: the close of hour 20 (market-on-close when it ends a session). The census book's sub-lots close at hours 10, 20 and 30.
  - [tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615] A forward-test book over the 1,838-name genome roster on completed hourly bars: when a Tensor black-square setup is confirmed by a green arrow within 3 bars, buy at the next hour's open and sell at the close of hour 20. The winner-census book trades the same deduplicated episodes in three equal sub-lots closing at hours 10, 20 and 30. Modeled cost 25.5 bp a side.
  - [tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615] - Exit: the close of hour 20 (market-on-close when it ends a session). The census book's sub-lots close at hours 10, 20 and 30.
- Sizing:
  - [tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615] 6. Sizing: one equal slot per event: the $100,000 book / (1,838 names x 1 timeframe) = about $54 (a third of it per census sub-lot); a lot is skipped when the book lacks the cash for its slot; modeled cost 25.5 bp a side (25 bp slippage + 0.5 bp fee per side in the code header, STUDY_SIDE_BPS = 25.5).
  - [tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615] Book capital $100,000; slot = book / (1,838 names x 1 timeframe) = about $54 per event (about $18 per census sub-lot); modeled cost 25.5 bp a side.
- Filters / data:
  - [tr-ro-tensor-1h-swing-v615] 3. Publication gate (card): only the bar just completed counts, and the roster's run publishes once at least half its names reach it.
- Parameters:
  - Horizons: 20 bars (1H Swing); 10 / 20 / 30 bars (winner census sub-lots).
- Variant axes (catalog): [{"Book": "1H Swing", "Exit": "one lot, at the close of hour 20", "Row": "`ro_tensor_1h_swing_v615`"}, {"Book": "Winner census", "Exit": "three equal sub-lots, at the closes of hours 10, 20 and 30", "Row": "`ro_winner_census_10_20_30`"}, {"Book": "1H Swing", "Exit": "one lot, at the close of hour 20", "Row": "`ro_tensor_1h_swing_v615`"}, {"Book": "Winner census", "Exit": "three equal sub-lots, at the closes of hours 10, 20 and 30", "Row": "`ro_winner_census_10_20_30`"}]

  - [r19-timing-hourly] Exits are evaluated before entries, in this order in the engine: - Observed bid at or below the stop: observed_stop_trigger. - Observed bid at or above the target: observed_target. - A scheduled time exit if a stored exit_at has passed. - The original 20 native bar deadline: 20 hourly bars after signal_end (deadline_bars = 20).

  - [R19_TIMING_HOUR_FLOOR1_DELAY0] Exit evaluation in desk3/aster_batch15.py::_eval_timing, before entries, for every non-zero position: bid is the sell quote, else the last close of the kind's timeframe. In order: if stop is set and bid <= stop, exit reason `observed_stop_trigger`; else if target is set and bid >= target, exit reason `observed_target`; else if exit_at is set and now >= exit_at, exit reason `scheduled_time_exit`; else (hourly only) if 20 native bars have ended after the position's signal_end, exit reason `original_20_native_bar_deadline`. Any exit suppresses entries that cycle. Exit intents are market day sell_to_close unless a sleeve-specific rule below states otherwise. 7. Stop floor: floorstop = min(stop,
  - [R19_TIMING_HOUR_FLOOR1_DELAY0] Exit evaluation in desk3/aster_batch15.py::_eval_timing, before entries, for every non-zero position: bid is the sell quote, else the last close of the kind's timeframe.   - [R19_TIMING_HOUR_FLOOR1_DELAY0] Engine SPECS: kind hourly, floor 1, delay 0, risk 0.0025, notional 0.1, fee_bps 5, slots 8 (see Full algorithm).
  - [R19_TIMING_HOUR_FLOOR1_DELAY0] Entry sizing (all timing kinds): fee = fee_bps / 10000; budget = min(cash, 10000.0 * notional); qty = floor(budget / (price * (1 + fee))); if a stop exists, qty = min(qty, floor(10000.0 * risk / (price - stop))). Refuse if qty <= 0. At most slots=8 held-plus-new positions, one per symbol, symbols scanned in UNIVERSE42 order. Only the bar just completed counts, and the roster's run publishes once at least half its names reach it. Entry: the next hour's open, a market order within that hour; skipped once it has passed.

The only designed exit is time: a position is sold in full when the current panel bar index minus its entry bar index reaches 20 native (hourly) bars; late observation still exits. The exit price is the latest bar close on the sleeve's timeframe when available. No price stop and no profit target in the source policy.
- Sizing:
  - [H1STATE] 6. Sizing: budget = min(0.10 * equity, 0.01 * DV20, cash); shares = floor(budget / (execution price * 1.001)); shares < 1 emits nothing. Orders are buy entries at the execution price.
- Filters / data:
  - [H1STATE] Entry (exits first; if any exit intent is emitted the call returns exits only), from desk3/aster_batch1.py SPEC kind='tensor', frame='1h', cadence_s=3600: a symbol needs at least a 4-bar panel on the 1h frame. Repair test on the last 4 bars: balance[-1] - balance[0] >= 2 (balance = bullish votes minus bearish votes over the 7 vote channels stoch, aroon, di, obv, squeeze, pivot, wave); at least 2 of the 7 vote channels strictly increase across at least one adjacent transition in the panel; total_votes == 7 at both panel ends; the latest row's native status, when present, must be 'ready'. Price/volume gates on the latest panel row: close >= 5, dollar_volume20 >= 1,000,000, atr14 > 0. Warmup: t
- Parameters:
  - From `docs/ASTER_TENSOR_H1_RECOVERY-ALGORITHM.md` in this repo (derived from `desk3/aster_batch1.py`), in evaluation order. SPEC: kind="tensor", frame="1h", tf="1Hour", cadence_s=3600, session="rth". Inputs (INPUTS_BY_KIND["tensor"]): tensor, bars, positions. Vote channels (7): stoch, aroon, di, obv, squeeze, pivot, wave; a panel row's balance is bullish votes minus bearish votes (or the row's own balance field); excluded symbols: SPY, QQQ, B, GOLD. At most 10 positions held. The sleeve consumes canonical Tensor products via view["tensor"]; no tensor key in the snapshot means the sleeve is UNF

Options book: the Variance Value rule (as O6) on its share of the book. - Sizing:
  - [apex-c7-council] Sizing: Fixed shares of equity, the options book's T-bills = its share less its options' value. Options decide once a session in the last 45 minutes (15:15-15:45 ET): the listed QQQ monthly and strike nearest the model's, whole contracts (under one skipped), a structure as one multi-leg package, marketable limits. Exposure books market-on-close; Bitcoin in the last 10 minutes of the equity session; a $1,000,000 book.

The live QQQ quote and option chain; a model surface from VXN and the VIX 9-day / 3-month / 6-month ratios at today's levels; Black-Scholes with a 0.55% dividend. (Per the card.)
- Parameters:
  - Nasdaq book: N6, ½ × (APEX-50F target + GESTALT leverage), with the 0.20 band.
  - Gold book: gold futures' trend score × min(2, 20% / HAR volatility), 0.20 band, held as GLD.

Hourly: an edge in the last 5 closed regular-hours bars, ≥ 160 bars, ≥ 20 bars after the last signal; scans at :10, buys at :40, 10:00-15:59 ET.
- Exit rules:
  - [femto-blowoff] Daily: sold once 19 bars have closed after entry (the 20th session); backstop 28 days. No stop. - Hourly: sold 20 hourly bars after the bar that follows the signal; backstop 4 days. No stop.
  - [femto-blowoff] - Daily: sold once 19 bars have closed after entry (the 20th session); backstop 28 days. No stop. - Hourly: sold 20 hourly bars after the bar that follows the signal; backstop 4 days. No stop.
- Sizing:
  - [femto-blowoff] Fill law: budget = 30% of the book less held and working notional, split over the staged buys; whole shares at a fresh mid plus cost, at least 1; at most 10 positions.

- Trades: US equities — 411-stock Galath universe (Signal Prism US 413 without its two crypto pairs)
- Timeframe: 1d · 5m session tape
- Created by / source: Galath / GrokBot desk, bottom screen v1.0
- Description (from source records): Sector-first bottom
- Algorithm status: **FULL**
- Algorithm sources consulted: Test catalog entry/variants, Test strategies/galath/galath-sector-first-bottom.md, docs/SECTOR_FIRST_BOTTOM-RECREATE.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test strategies/galath/galath-sector-first-bottom.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test (main) strategies/galath/galath-sector-first-bottom.md — section '## Exit', Test docs/SECTOR_FIRST_BOTTOM-RECREATE.md, Test strategies/galath/galath-sector-first-bottom.md (Entry section), 2026-10-31 algorithm audit cure A (findings b1-entry, b2-exit, b3-sizing, b5-reconcile; quotes verbatim from cited sources)

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [galath-sector-first-bottom] Bottom screen on the scan's daily bars: single names (no index products), ≥ $8, 20-day dollar volume ≥ $15M, no > 70% 60-day collapse. Points: quality (above 45% of the 200-day, no > 45% 60-day drop, ≥ $25M volume), cheap (18-55% off the 52-week high, 3-28% under the 200-day), sector (lagging SPY over 126 days, leading over 20; its ETF turning), structure (a contracting base, a spring), a selling climax, impulse (on the 21-day under the 50-day, the 21-day rising). BUY at ≥ 8 points with ≥ 2 turn points (structure, climax, impulse), cheap ≥ 1 and quality ≥ 2; under 9 points it waits while SPY is under its 200-day with a new 20-day low, or the tape is risk-off. Sector: waterfall, trend and tro
  - [galath-sector-first-bottom] Sector-first bottom. It buys a cheap, liquid stock basing under its long averages when its sector has turned against SPY, on the next-support plan. Asset class US equities. Timeframe 1d with a 5m session tape. Universe: the 411-stock universe described in the card (Signal Prism US 413 without its two crypto pairs). Status in the card: waiting.
- Exit rules:
  - [galath-sector-first-bottom] The plan's stop and target ride as an engine-held bracket. - Trims: 20% when price is rejected at the first Fib above the buy (38.2 / 50 / 61.8% of the 90-day range) with the gain under 35%; half after +50% within 8 days, or at a weekly RSI ≥ 68 with a daily bearish divergence after +80%. - One add when price is back within 2% of the 50- or 200-day EMA after 5 of the prior 16 closes below it. - A position worth under $75 is sold.
  - [galath-sector-first-bottom] 2. Points. Quality: above 45% of the 200-day, no > 45% 60-day drop, at least $25M volume. Cheap: 18 to 55% off the 52-week high, 3 to 28% under the 200-day. Sector: lagging SPY over 126 days, leading over 20 days, its ETF turning. Structure: a contracting base, a spring. A selling climax. Impulse: on the 21-day under the 50-day, the 21-day rising.
  - [galath-sector-first-bottom] - The plan's stop and target ride as an engine-held bracket. - Trims: 20% when price is rejected at the first Fib above the buy (38.2 / 50 / 61.8% of the 90-day range) with the gain under 35%; half after +50% within 8 days, or at a weekly RSI ≥ 68 with a daily bearish divergence after +80%. - One add when price is back within 2% of the 50- or 200-day EMA after 5 of the prior 16 closes below it. - A position worth under $75 is sold.
- Sizing:
  - [galath-sector-first-bottom] Sizing: 1.5% of equity at risk to the stop (2% of price without one), capped at 8% of equity; whole shares.
- Filters / data:
  - [galath-sector-first-bottom] 4. Sector filter: waterfall, trend and trough sectors and names without a sector ETF are skipped; cyclicals wait in a risk-off tape.
- Parameters:
  - Bottom screen on the scan's daily bars: single names (no index products), ≥ $8, 20-day dollar volume ≥ $15M, no > 70% 60-day collapse.
  - Points: quality (above 45% of the 200-day, no > 45% 60-day drop, ≥ $25M volume), cheap (18-55% off the 52-week high, 3-28% under the 200-day), sector (lagging SPY over 126 days, leading over 20; its ETF turning), structure (a contracting base, a spring), a selling climax, impulse (on the 21-day under the 50-day, the 21-day rising).
  - BUY at ≥ 8 points with ≥ 2 turn points (structure, climax, impulse), cheap ≥ 1 and quality ≥ 2; under 9 points it waits while SPY is under its 200-day with a new 20-day low, or the tape is risk-off.

## Parallax

- Type: other | Family: griffith | Style evidence (catalog): Multi-engine swing
- Trades: US equities — SCOPE universe: 550 US names
- Timeframe: 1d
- Created by / source: Griffith / Ledge desk, Parallax PX_1_3_0_EXACT (conditional lane PX_1_3_0_CHALLENGER)
- Description (from source records): Parallax
- Algorithm status: **FULL**
- Algorithm sources consulted: Test catalog entry/variants, Test docs/GRIFFITH_PARALLAX-RECREATE.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test docs/GRIFFITH_PARALLAX-RECREATE.md, dwj9ddyvf6-hub/Test (main) docs/GRIFFITH_PARALLAX-RECREATE.md — section '## Exit', docs/GRIFFITH_PARALLAX-RECREATE.md, Test docs/GRIFFITH_PARALLAX-RECREATE.md (Configuration section), 2026-10-31 algorithm audit cure A (findings b1-entry, b2-exit, b3-sizing, b5-reconcile; quotes verbatim from cited sources)

### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [griffith-parallax] Decision: once a trading day before the open (else at the session's first pass), on the last completed bars, through the source's orchestrator over the universe. Field: each sector ETF against SPY (10-, 20- and 126-day relative strength, its 126-day percentile among the sectors, the EMA 50 slope) reads WATERFALL, TURN, TROUGH or TREND; names outside the sector map read TURN; a WATERFALL or unreadable field gives no decision. Regime: across the universe, the median day, the share up over 20 days, the median ATR% and the spread of 20-day returns give PANIC, REFLEXIVE_REBOUND, HIGH_VOLATILITY_DELEVERAGING, ORDERLY_RISK_ON, NARROW_RISK_ON or RANGE_BOUND; the medians of 5-, 20- and 60-day returns
- Exit rules:
  - [griffith-parallax] Brackets: DRIFT -1.5 / +2.5 ATR, RECLAIM -1.25 / +2.25 ATR, DISLOCATION -1.5 / +2.25 ATR; COMPRESSION a stop 0.25 ATR under the compression low and a target 2.5 × the risk; the conditional lane keeps those stops with a target 2.5 × the risk.
  - [griffith-parallax] - Brackets: DRIFT -1.5 / +2.5 ATR, RECLAIM -1.25 / +2.25 ATR, DISLOCATION -1.5 / +2.25 ATR; COMPRESSION a stop 0.25 ATR under the compression low and a target 2.5 × the risk; the conditional lane keeps those stops with a target 2.5 × the risk.
- Sizing:
  - [griffith-parallax] Sizing: risk 0.35% (conditional lane 0.5%) of equity / risk per share, within the strategy's 3% risk cap less open and armed risk; per order <= 35% of equity and <= 98% of buying power; a held name is not added to; $100,000 book.
- Filters / data:
  - [griffith-parallax] 5. BUY gate: opportunity = engine score less penalties (ATR over 4%, thin or heavy volume, a large shock, a stretch over EMA 20) >= 48; relative volume >= 2.8 is AVOID; a PANIC or HIGH_VOLATILITY_DELEVERAGING regime or a TROUGH field is WAIT.
  - [griffith-parallax] Decision: once a trading day before the open (else at the session's first pass), on the last completed bars, through the source's orchestrator over the universe. Field: each sector ETF against SPY (10-, 20- and 126-day relative strength, its 126-day percentile among the sectors, the EMA 50 slope) reads WATERFALL, TURN, TROUGH or TREND; names outside the sector map read TURN; a WATERFALL or unreadable field gives no decision. Regime: across the universe, the median day, the share up over 20 days, the median ATR% and the spread of 20-day returns give PANIC, REFLEXIVE_REBOUND, HIGH_VOLATILITY_DELEVERAGING, ORDERLY_RISK_ON, NARROW_RISK_ON or RANGE_BOUND; the medians of 5-, 20- and 60-day returns
- Parameters:
  - Own parameters: opportunity >= 48, relative volume >= 2.8 = AVOID, field engine bonus +6, risk 0.35% (lane 0.5%), strategy risk cap 3%, per-order caps 35% of equity / 98% of buying power, arm 2 days (compression 7; lane 3, compression 5).

  - [mk-atrlevelcascade] ATR level cascade (SPY): an intraday trade sequence that enters at each successive ATR level of the day ladder and targets the next level, in both directions. ### Detailed algorithm
- Signal / entry rules:
  - [aster_saty_research] Exits are evaluated first; if any exit is emitted the evaluation returns with no entry. No entry at or after 15:40 ET, after 3 entries today, or when the day's realised result is at or below -2R. A fresh two-sided SPY quote is required: the quote timestamp must be within 5 seconds of now (and not in the future), else the evaluation fails closed. Price is the quote mid, else the last 10-minute bar close. Open risk is summed over held positions as qty x |avg_price - invalidation|; a new entry is refused when open risk plus the new 1R would exceed the 1R correlated cap. A candidate must be a dict for SPY, with SPY not held, and with positive net room both at its planned entry and at the current
- Exit rules:
  - [aster_saty_research] Structural invalidation: the current price at or past the position's invalidation (at or below for a long, at or above for a short) sells/buys back the full position. - Final exit deadline: at or after 15:50 ET any held position is closed in full. - Target-1 scale: an unscaled position whose price reaches its first target is half closed (the full quantity when halving would give 0). - Trail after scale: a scaled position whose price returns to its entry reference is closed in full (trail to breakeven after scale). - Exits are market, day, sell_to_close (or buy_to_close for a short) intents.
